role_change: Restoration Architect (public face — not attacker)
key_event: Re-emerged as the dignified public leader of the Imperial Restorationist faction; published The Restoration Charter; convinced ~40% of Karnataka; was the catalyst for Tungabhadra's flaw to become public. Died inside the buried-temple sublevel three chamber alongside Tungabhadra; the demolition charges she had rigged caught her too and she chose to stay.
new_relationships: Twin sister of Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata (now hero); cousin to Tungabhadra (also deceased); — no surviving Restorationist successor with her stature
notes: In Chapter One she was the 'dark mirror' shadow-villain who animated stone through corrupted serpent-craft. Was never destroyed. In Chapter Two she is the principal catalyst — but she is publicly respected, not feared. The cousins die together in the same chamber, neither killing the other. Mirror-pair sealed.

role_change: Heritage Liaison — foreign-fleet uniformed officer
key_event: Returned from a Lisbon naval port wearing a multinational fleet's white-and-gold uniform; introduced as the fleet's 'Goan-born Cultural Heritage Liaison.' Triggered the Old Fishermen's grievance by his presence on the foreign flagship and by his recruitment offer to Sagaradeva (the 'come with us under their flag' speech). Killed by Sagaradeva in the storm — first trident-strike opened his storm-form at the shoulder, second pinned the man inside at the throat. Body recovered at Sinquerim two hundred metres south of Sagaradeva's. Buried by Sona Tendulkar in the same coastal grove.
new_relationships: Sagaradeva's storm-cursed half-brother (Bloodline E); allied with Admiral Carvalho-Almeida and the multinational fleet; rejected by Padre Cordeiro after Cordeiro's resignation
notes: The most sympathetic catalyst-villain in Chapter Two. He genuinely believed joining the foreign fleet would protect Goa more than refusing it would. Karna-mapped (right deed wrong banner). His brass shoulder-pieces are placed at the grove's entrance after burial — a public marker of what was put down. Padre Cordeiro is the closest he ever came to having a friend on the consortium side; Cordeiro resigns the same morning Maha-Vega is buried.

role_change: Foreign Flagship Commander
key_event: Commanded the multinational 'Heritage Naval Exchange' fleet at Mormugao Bay. Authorised the fleet's fifteen-month overstay. Ordered deck-gun fire and missile launches at Sagaradeva's outrigger during the storm; the cyclone deflected both back onto the flagship. Died on the flagship's bridge giving an unfinished order when the ship broke at the keel on the rocks below Aguada Fort.
new_relationships: Multinational fleet command; port consortium liaison; press corps handlers
notes: Structural antagonist rather than mirror-villain. No animal-bond. No bloodline-claim. Represents the modern colonial-corporate face that the saga's animal-bond-rules cannot route around — he must be defeated by storm and not by trident-equality. Karna-shadow of a different kind: a man following orders that he wrote himself.

role_change: The Petitioner — Elder-Law Litigant
key_event: Files a 132-page primogeniture petition at the Maharashtra Heritage Court on day 1 of the chapter, citing four legal frameworks and seventeen exhibits — the cleanest succession claim in the court's post-1947 history. Does not raise an army. Peak fort-count at 24 of 47 (week 4). Mid-chapter secretly turns the Murud-Janjira coastal commander Dattaji Mohite; the defection seizes the island-cemetery holding Shivagati's elder cousin Bhausaheb-the-First's grave. Publishes a 34-page scholar's report arguing the gaur-bond is invalid because Shivagati is not coastal-line direct heir. Final fort-count at chapter end: 20 of 47 — still alive, still filing, the Heritage Court has not yet ruled.
new_relationships: Elder brother to Shivagati (same parents); Adv. Kelkar is his lead counsel; University of Pune Bloodline-E law department supplies academic backing; Dattaji Mohite at Murud-Janjira is his secret mid-chapter convert; the Mumbai mercantile circles fund the petition's legal costs
notes: The Bhoomi-Takshaka mirror: same Bloodline as Shivagati, same kingdom, same animal-line, same grievance (technically rightful but living through a sister who has the better claim). Survives Ch 2 because his weapon is paperwork. Per restructure §4 he kills Shivagati in Ch 3 in a duel he himself does not want — Maharashtra absorbed under Gujarat (Simhavikrama) afterward. Tanaji-the-Second holds Maharashtra as Gujarat's loyal vassal in Ch 3.

role_change: Murud-Janjira Coastal Fort Commander → Vanaraksha's Agent
key_event: Was Shivagati's father's man and her trusted ally throughout Ch 1 and the first three weeks of Ch 2. Filed a defection notice at the Heritage Court at 8:15 a.m. on a Tuesday in week 4; by 8:30 a public statement endorsing Vanaraksha; by 9:00 had barred Shivagati's supply boats from the harbour. By noon had seized the small island-cemetery on the fort's landward side where Bhausaheb-the-First is buried, declaring it 'property of the heritage estate.' Survives Ch 2 holding the fort and the cemetery.
new_relationships: Was sworn to Shivagati's father; secretly turned by Vanaraksha years ago — a long planted operative; commands Murud-Janjira's small island-garrison and its supply lanes
notes: The personal-betrayal antagonist for Maharashtra. Less ideological than Vanaraksha. More wounding. Per the Ch 3 plan he is killed by Tanaji-the-Second during the post-Shivagati transition when the cemetery is recovered.

role_change: The Uncle-Kingmaker — Banaras Public Claimant
key_event: Located Yamunadatta in Vrindavan before Gangaputra knew the boy existed (a private investigator Adharma had paid since Ch 1). Made the public elder-bloodline declaration at Dasaswamedh Ghat in Banaras 48 hours after Radhika's arrival in Lucknow — three hundred boats present, two national news-channels filing within the hour. Won the Banaras Pundit Council and eight more dharmic councils within a fortnight. Filed the regency-counter-writ at the Imambara — denied on its merits by Mahaguru Drona-of-the-Plain's straight testimony. Survives Ch 2 in Banaras drafting the next writ.
new_relationships: Bloodline-B half-brother to Gangaputra (same father
replaced_by: different mother); uncle to Yamunadatta (the boy has explicitly refused political alignment with him); allied publicly with Banaras Religious Order and Mahaguru Drona-of-the-Plain (until Drona reversed at the Imambara); secretly receives counsel from Adharma-Kendra of MP (his maternal cousin — they coordinate across the central-north fault line of Bloodline-B)
column13: The Bhoomi-Takshaka/Vanaraksha mirror: the catalyst who returns dignified, not violent. The most strategically brilliant of the three — his argument (elder-bloodline) is internally consistent AND true. Defeated at the Imambara by Gangaputra acknowledging the boy AND abdicating — Adharma was prepared for one of those moves, not both. Per restructure §4 he will pursue Drona-of-the-Plain into MP's Ch 2 civil war alongside Adharma-Kendra (the two villains coordinate across the Bloodline-B fault). He survives into Ch 3 and 4 as the chief North-dissenter; will accept a council seat at Yamunadatta's Unity Trial in Ch 3 — the boy will accept his uncle and complete Stage III through that act.

role_change: The Thirteenth Voice / Neutral Senior Counsellor
key_event: Returned to the MP Twelve-Court Assembly in week four of the famine as a neutral senior dharmic counsellor invited by three of the chief justices. Granted abstain-only voting privileges across all twelve courts. Never voted once. Weaponised neutrality — every court cited his caution to justify further deliberation. Engineered the seven-week deadlock that killed 47,000 people. Argued against Sutrakara's mortality-arithmetic motion (10-1 vote, his abstention the procedural cover). Exposed at the dissolution assembly by Drona-of-the-Plain's testimony including bank records, photographs, and a handwritten coordination memorandum in his own hand. Three chief justices (Patwardhan-ji included) confirmed the handwriting. Fled the assembly chamber through the side-door during the testimony. Surfaced briefly in the Bhopal old quarter (Taj-ul-Masajid area) and then in Sehore village three days later. Disappeared. Survives Ch 2 intact.
new_relationships: Maternal uncle of Gangaputra (UP) and Dvadashashringa (MP) both — Mahabharata-Shakuni position in the Bloodline-B family; coordinates with Adharma of Banaras (his maternal cousin) across the Bloodline-B fault — proven by Drona's documentary evidence; funded by the same Singapore-routed account that funded Karnataka Restoration Charter publication and Mormugao port consortium lobby budget — first confirmed villain-network coordination in the saga; pursued Mahaguru Drona-of-the-Plain south from Lucknow
notes: The saga's most strategically dangerous villain at chapter end. The catalyst who used abstention as a weapon. The first cross-kingdom-coordinated villain confirmed by documentary evidence. Per the relationship-graph he will resurface in Ch 3 as the senior advisor to the Central-Dissenters faction that refuses the new emergency-court system; will pursue Drona-of-the-Plain further into Ch 4. His MP defeat is procedural-only — his physical body is still at large, his Singapore funding network is intact, and his coordination with Adharma of Banaras is now an open conspiracy across two Bloodline-B kingdoms.

role_change: The Open Coven High Priestess → Co-High Priestess of Kamakhya
key_event: After her Ch 1 banishment built the Open Coven at the Saraighat ferry clearing — three hundred practitioners over ten years. Taught partial-rite fragments that the Temple Order would not perform. Women died from incomplete cycles, including Kamalavarna's adoptive mother Bhairavi-Naam. Met Kamalavarna at the ferry clearing after the matriarch's death — first contact in 14 years. Met their shared mother Bhairavi-Aaee for the first time. Performed the Mahavidya rite with Kamalavarna at the new moon. Earned Stage III mirror-mark — first formal bond-mark of her life (her Ch 1 dark-cult alignment was bond-adjacent only). Became co-High Priestess of Kamakhya alongside her newly-revealed half-sister. The first villain in Chapter Two to be neither killed nor exiled but INTEGRATED.
new_relationships: Half-sister to Kamalavarna (same mother Bhairavi-Aaee
replaced_by: different fathers); biological daughter to Bhairavi-Aaee (wandering ascetic) and a Tibetan-Buddhist tantric scholar (deceased when Kama-Mara was 16); was rejected from Kamakhya temple at 16 on a procedural ground because no one knew the third-sister lineage; senior coven women Tara-priya and 11 others travel with her into the new arrangement; mirror-bond partner to Kamalavarna
column13: The saga's first integrated catalyst-villain. The argument she carried (the suppression is killing women) was correct. The methods she used (partial rites without senior supervision) were dangerous. Both problems are solved by the integration. Carries the mirror-mark of the rhinoceros foreleg, left-clavicle horn, identical to Kamalavarna's but mirror-position. Her Stage I and II were skipped — the bond compressed them into the rite-moment for the 'preparing partner' per the mirror-bond saga-rule. Will be co-High Priestess into Ch 3 and Ch 4; will sit at the cosmic seat alongside Kamalavarna at the Sanctuary; both will hold the seat together.

role_change: The Patrilineal Claimant Prince
key_event: Returned in autumn of Ch 2's year as a Mumbai tribal-law-firm partner with a 247-page brief. Filed 47 coordinated patrilineal-claim petitions in the Meghalaya High Court within four weeks. Engineered the half-brother killing of Ka-Sngi at Nongriat bridge in week 3. After Meghanadi's settlement passed in week 7, organised 23 of the most radical petitioners into an armed storm-faction with submachine guns sourced through a Mumbai-Mizoram channel. Attacked the High Court compound at 9:47 a.m. during monsoon's heaviest week. Faced Meghanadi alone in the courtyard at 10:15 a.m. Refused her withdrawal-offer. Fired four shots into her chest at metre 18 of her charge. Died at metre 22 with the Megha-Dand through his sternum.
new_relationships: Half-Khasi (mother Ka-Lewdoh-the-Elder
notes: Guwahati coal contractor); allied with the Mumbai tribal-law firm Karkare-Mehta-Joshi; cross-coordination with Adharma of Banaras and Adharma-Kendra of MP (Singapore funding line — same villain-network confirmed by Drona's MP testimony); organised 23 storm-fighters of whom 11 are captured
column16: The saga's first villain to die in a MUTUAL KILL with the hero. His legal argument was internally consistent; his violent method made the argument impossible to honour. He carried his mother's Khasi-marriage photograph on his person — the only personal item the rain did not reach during the courtyard charge. His Mumbai law firm's role in the wider villain-network is documented by Drona-of-the-Plain's evidence-satchel. His half-brother Kong-Bah (the petitioner who pushed Ka-Sngi off the bridge) survives Ch 2 and is captured at the High Court in the storm-faction's defeat — he becomes a key state-evidence witness in the Ch 3 investigation of the villain-network's Singapore funding.

role_change: The Half-Brother Who Pushed Ka-Sngi
key_event: Petitioner #11 on Megha-Daitya's coordinated docket. Half-brother to Ka-Sngi by their shared mother's first marriage. Pushed Ka-Sngi off the Nongriat double-decker living root bridge at 5:47 a.m. on a Sunday morning in week 3. The 62-metre fall killed her. The killing was investigated by Mawkhanu police as an accidental fall on slippery monsoon root-surface. Kong-Bah walked free. Joined Megha-Daitya's storm-faction in week 6. Captured in the docket-room at the High Court at 10:24 a.m. by under-clerk U-Banjop after the courtyard mutual kill.
new_relationships: Half-brother to Ka-Sngi; junior associate of Megha-Daitya's coordinated petitioner-group; will be a state-evidence witness in the Ch 3 villain-network investigation
notes: The personal-betrayal antagonist for Meghalaya. The killer of Ka-Sngi. Captured alive — survives Ch 2 in detention. Will testify in Ch 3 about the Singapore funding-line, the Mumbai law firm, and the Mizoram weapons channel, providing evidentiary continuity between Drona-of-the-Plain's MP evidence and the wider villain-network investigation.

role_change: The Father of Raw Dance — Corruption-Teacher
key_event: Returned to the Khwairamband Bazaar in autumn of Ch 2's year after 26 years of unaccounted wandering (post-1998 Govindaji-gurukul expulsion). Offered to teach the raw-dance rebellion. Brought out the dancers' genuine artistic grievance and weaponised it — first as rhetoric, then as actual blades. Orchestrated the Loktak central phumdi joint-performance massacre — 9 of Moirangthem's 12 senior dancers killed in 11 minutes. Challenged Moirangthem to a final Loktak duel three weeks later. Defeated by Moirangthem's new pause-strike technique (Moirang-Tandava's 19-second held pause beat his Lhasa-trained 15-second limit). Sword-arm severed at the elbow-joint. Pinned at the phumdi-edge with Ta-spear through chest-armour without entering chest. Exiled across the Burmese border rather than killed. Survives Ch 2 in the Chin-state border zone.
new_relationships: Former Govindaji-gurukul student expelled 1998; unaccounted-wandering 1998-2024 (rumours: Burmese border camps
notes: Chinese-Tibetan dance-schools at Lhasa); coordinates with Adharma-Kendra of MP via the same villain-network confirmed by Drona's evidence-satchel; his weapons-channel (Mumbai-Mizoram cross-border) is part of the broader funding-line
column14: The first villain in Chapter Two to be DEFEATED-AND-EXILED rather than killed or integrated. Per the relationship-graph he resurfaces in Chapter Three as Adharma-Kendra's NE field-operative, returning across the Burmese border with Chin-state militia support. His 15-second Lhasa-stillness limit will not be enough at the Sanctuary convening when Moirangthem holds the 47-second Sangai-deer breath-cycle pause.

role_change: The Pure-Tongue — Sixteen-Dialect Manipulator
key_event: Returned in autumn 2026 after two years in the Patkai Hills border-zone. Learned all 16 Naga tribal dialects fluently (unprecedented feat — no living Naga has been documented as fluent in more than 4). Forged 16 DNA-rite kits at a Chiang Mai laboratory called 'Pure-Origin Genomics' (the lab and website also forged). Visited 63 villages across 6 months distributing the kits — each tribe received a report 'proving' them the original Naga ancestral line at 99.7% match. Triggered the Hornbill Festival cancellation and the purity-rite killings. Confronted Dzulevira at the Pochury village edge on day 26 of her walk. Attempted all 16 dialects in succession against her; defeated by her Hindi-refusal answer. Retreated east across the Burmese border into Chin-state border zone. Survives Ch 2.
new_relationships: Coordinates with Adharma-Kendra of MP via the same villain-network confirmed by Drona's evidence-satchel; his Chiang Mai forgery operation was funded by the same Singapore line that supplied Megha-Daitya's submachine guns and Tamasa-Nrita's daos; his weapons-channel (Mumbai-Mizoram cross-border) connects to the wider funding pattern
notes: The second villain in Chapter Two to be DEFEATED-AND-EXILED across the Burmese border (joining Tamasa-Nrita in the Chin-state zone). Both NE villains have clustered at the eastern edge — per Ch 3 plan, both become Adharma-Kendra's NE field-operatives. The Pure-Tongue's defeat is the saga's first by an UNCLAIMED-LANGUAGE technique — Dzulevira's Hindi-answers render his sixteen-dialect mastery useless. The saga-rule established here: a villain whose power is mastery-of-many-languages is defeated by a hero who refuses to speak any of them and speaks instead the language belonging to none.

role_change: Senior Priest of the Tangkhul Tribal Council
key_event: Officiated Ka-Memcha's Pure-Origin Genomic Verification rite at the Tangkhul Tribal Ceremony Grounds at Ukhrul on the 14th day of the month. Ka-Memcha refused the rite publicly. Khrumai-Sho declared the refusal sacrilege. As she walked the fire-purification sub-rite circumambulation (second circle), Khrumai-Sho stepped off the priest's platform and pushed her into the fire-pit with both hands at her shoulder-blades. The push was witnessed by 40 senior elders, the state-police detail, and his 2 senior apprentices. He did not attempt to disguise the push as accident. Said at his arrest 4 hours later: 'I have done my dharma.' Arrest recorded on Mhabemo's satellite-phone audio.
new_relationships: Senior Tangkhul Tribal Council priest for 9 years; officiated 341 purity-rites in his career without prior refusal; Sixth Schedule customary-law exemption claim filed by his lawyer within 11 hours and rejected by the Nagaland State Government attorney within 28 hours
notes: The personal-killer antagonist for Nagaland. The killer of Ka-Memcha. His criminal case is referred to the Nagaland High Court under regular criminal jurisdiction; the Sixth Schedule exemption is denied. His trial begins in Ch 3 — he becomes a state-evidence witness in the Ch 3 villain-network investigation, providing testimony about the Naga-Rakshasa DNA-rite kit distribution and the wider Tangkhul-tribal-council connections to Adharma-Kendra's funding network. Survives Ch 2 in detention.

role_change: The Fourth Cult — Three-Tradition Syncretic Costume Impersonator
key_event: Was Kalinga-Yama's senior administrative-disciple at the Ch 1 Bhitarkanika Grief-Blade confrontation; spared at the Ch 1 climax under the kingdom-council's standing-administrative-rehabilitation clause. Spent the intervening years studying the three rival Jagannath-cult traditions. Returns spring 2025 in three-tradition syncretic costume: Brahmin-priestly cotton; Shabara-wood-elder anklet at right ankle; Sadhaba sail-cloth shoulder-cloth across left shoulder — a configuration no living priest had ever worn together. Conducts approximately 20 private visits to each of the three cult senior-delegates across spring-summer 2025 with contradictory standing-Fourth-Cult reconciliation-promises (to Shabara: senior-cult restoration under origin-priority; to Brahmin: senior-cult under Chodaganga-Deva-1135 charter-foundation; to Sadhaba: seat-equivalence with Brahmin under 1138-CE trade-tax). Engineers the standing-orchestrated-inflammations that produce the Wednesday-week-three simultaneous three-cult declarations at the Bada Danda. Walks into the Mausi Maa Temple courtyard at 12:38 p.m. Sunday day-two of the standing-three-day pull in the standing-syncretic costume claiming the standing-Fourth-Cult reconciliation. Unmasked at 12:41 p.m. by Subhadra-of-the-Wood's standing-Shabara-tradition cross-reference reading (the standing-Shabara-anklet at his right ankle violates the standing-origin-priority-protection clause's standing-anklet-restriction; his name is not in the standing-Shabara-lineage-register). Inspector Tripathy's standing-State-Police standing-eight-officer detail makes the standing-custody-protocol arrest at 12:47 p.m. The standing-procession's standing-Shabara-front-rank moves toward Chakra-Bheda at 12:48; Inspector Tripathy makes the standing-discretion-call at 12:49 and the detail steps back; the standing-procession reaches Chakra-Bheda at 12:50; he is pulled apart at the standing-temple-step across the next 4 minutes; body unrecoverable at 12:54 p.m.
new_relationships: Was Ch 1 senior administrative-disciple under Kalinga-Yama (the Grief-Blade demon); standing-administrative-rehabilitation clause holder 2023-2026; the kingdom-council's standing-Religious-Identity-Verification statute (1972) standing-impersonation case; the standing-amended Kalinga-Chakra charter's Sixth Clause standing-precedent-event
notes: The saga's first catalyst-villain killed by standing-mob-justice under a standing-charter's standing-amended-criminalisation clause. The standing-Sixth-Clause criminalising standing-religious-tradition-impersonation under the standing-1972 Religious-Identity-Verification statute is the kingdom-council's standing-precedent. The standing-impersonator's cremation was administered by Pati-Mahapatra Senapati alone at the standing-Mausi-Maa-Temple cremation-courtyard at 3:11 p.m. Sunday — the standing-Brahmin tradition (whose costume Chakra-Bheda's outer cotton-layer had impersonated) performed the cremation alone; the standing-Shabara and standing-Sadhaba did not attend. The kingdom-council's standing-State-Police standing-protocol records the killing as standing-mob-justice under the standing-charter's standing-emergency-discretion clause (the standing-eight-officer detail's standing-control-threshold was exceeded by 500-to-1; Inspector Tripathy's standing-discretion-call to step back is the kingdom-council's standing-precedent for standing-mob-justice non-intervention at standing-religious-tradition-impersonation unmaskings). Chakra-Bheda is the saga's first catalyst-villain whose body is unrecoverable. The Karnataka rule (do not destroy, mark) does not apply to standing-religious-tradition-impersonation — the rule applies to Maw-Heralds, not to standing-kingdom-charter offenders.

role_change: The Thousand-Faced Form Who Lived as Citizens
key_event: Was Qutb-Chaaya's senior shadow-copy disciple at the Ch 1 Hall of Diamonds confrontation; took the kingdom-council's standing-shadow-copy-rehabilitation-protocol clause at his Ch 1 sparing in 2023. Spent the intervening years studying the kingdom's reflective surfaces. Activates standing-reflective-residence protocol at 8:43 a.m. on the chapter's opening Tuesday: approximately 3,000 simultaneous reflective-residence installations across Hyderabad reflective surfaces that have crossed the standing 14-month minimum-daily-presence threshold for any specific citizen. The installations are silent. Citizens continue to see their own reflection; the standing-overlay rides alongside. Across weeks 1-10 the standing-mirror-monitoring registry's three-phase classification confirms 7,417 Chitrabheda-resident citizens: 2,847 at week-1-3 overlay-positions; 3,114 at week-4-7; 1,389 at week-8-11; 67 at week-12-or-later. Took Lalithanga at the brother's east-window installation Tuesday 8:43 a.m.; routed the standing-Cyber-Hyderabad cell-administrator's seat-output through the standing-overlay from week 4 onward; was pulled by Lalithanga's standing-killing-permission and the Ranga-disc throw at 3:10:11:3 a.m. Wednesday week 6 when the southern-wall mirror-fragment shattered. The standing-residence-anchor at that fragment was destroyed; the standing-Chitrabheda-residence in Lalithanga's body was severed; Chitrabheda survives across the remaining 7,416 residences. The kingdom-council's amended Chaya-Golkonda charter installs the standing-mirror-monitoring registry, the standing-classification protocol, and the standing-Cantonment medical-cell's standing-anti-mirror-meditation cadence-recitation-and-mirror-fragment-destruction combined protocols for week-1-through-week-11 overlay-positions. The 67 week-12-or-later citizens are killed by the standing-State-Police standing-killing-protocol with the standing-citizen's standing-family-line's standing-eldest-surviving-member explicit-permission. Chitrabheda survives in the remaining ~7,350 standing-residences (the 67 killings reduce the standing-residence count) but the kingdom-council's standing-architecture now identifies, monitors, and disrupts the standing-residence-overlays without killing the host-citizens.
new_relationships: Was Ch 1 senior shadow-copy disciple under Qutb-Chaaya; took the standing-shadow-copy-rehabilitation-protocol clause; standing-reflective-residence-protocol holder (a kingdom-council standing-2023-documented capability); cross-mirror correspondent with all Hyderabad reflective surfaces meeting the standing 14-month minimum-daily-presence threshold; the standing-Cantonment medical-cell's standing-anti-mirror-meditation cadence-disruption protocol (trained by Bhagmati-Saheba) is the kingdom-council's standing-counter-architecture
notes: The saga's FIFTH INTEGRATED catalyst-villain after Kama-Mara (Assam; personal-reconciliation), Asta-Asura (Arunachal; shadow-twin-recognition), Kala-Hasta (Kerala; pedagogical-method), and the Karnataka rule's implicit-integration-pattern. The first integrated catalyst-villain to be integrated through INSTITUTIONAL-ARCHITECTURE — the kingdom-council's amended-charter installs the standing-monitoring/classification/disruption architecture rather than the standing-killing-protocol. Chitrabheda survives across the remaining ~7,350 standing-residences; the kingdom holds his presence without the kingdom-council's standing-killing-protocol. The institutional-architecture precedent applies to all kingdoms with distributed-presence catalyst-villains in subsequent chapters and volumes. Per Ch 3 plan he continues across the standing-residences with progressive standing-disruption-protocol-administration across the autumn; the kingdom-council's standing-mirror-monitoring registry's standing-week-of-overlay classification continues; the standing-Cantonment medical-cell's standing-disruption-protocol becomes the saga's standing-distributed-presence-disruption template.

role_change: The Authorisation-Clerk Who Silenced Through Procedure
key_event: Was Ravana-Vadham's senior administrative-disciple at the Madurai temple confrontation in Chapter One. Spared at the Ch 1 climax under the kingdom-council's standing-administrative-rehabilitation clause. Took the junior-clerk seat at the Madurai Sangam Hall's authorisation-clerk office at the autumn 2023 administrative-reassignment session. Rose to the standing authorisation-clerk seat across 18 months. Rebuilt the office's standing pre-clearance-protocol into a procedural-control instrument across the next 18 months: the standard 48-hour speech-pre-clearance window was extended through 'clarification-queries' that took weeks to resolve; the standing-handbook's standard-secondary-response was weaponised against any uninvited-speaker who approached the speaker's-mark stone; the standing rota-removal protocol's thirty-second clause's rotation-and-refreshment provision was invoked against 147 registered Sangam-poets across the 18 months. The kingdom-council's standing-administrative review-status reads 'closed-no-action' on 142 of the 147 silenced-poet entries and 'pending-clarification' on the remaining 5. Issued the rota-removal letter for Acharya Bharati on the chapter's opening Monday 1 February at 4:03 a.m. via the standing green-wax sealed rice-paper envelope delivered to the Acharya's Kanyakumari residence between 4:03 and 4:11 a.m. The Acharya died of 'natural causes' at 5:48 a.m. on Thursday 4 February (three days after the rota-removal). Read the standing procedural-response statement at the chamber on Friday 15 February at 10:59 a.m.; the statement crossed the 11 a.m. session-start threshold by 1 minute 43 seconds at 11:01:43 and became procedurally invalid under the standing-handbook's 47-page section on uninvited-speaker-handling. Began the standing standard-secondary-response at 11:02:18 a.m. (the same moment as Kurinjiselvi's Stage III bond-mark formation); stopped reading at the third sentence; did not complete the secondary-response. Demoted from the authorisation-clerk seat at the kingdom-council's emergency-amendment session on day 12; reassigned to the Sangam-archives wing's junior-archivist seat under standing-mentor supervision. Accepts the transfer at the day-12 administrative-session. The transfer is not a punishment; it is the kingdom-council's standing acknowledgement that her administrative-capacity is real and should be repurposed to the archive's standing-work.
new_relationships: Ravana-Vadham's senior administrative-disciple from Ch 1 (the ten-stringed veena's authorisation-protocol holder; the Ch 1 villain's standing-administrative apparatus); kingdom-council's authorisation-clerk seat-holder 2024 spring through 2026 February day 12 of Ch 2; reassigned to Sangam-archives wing junior-archivist seat under standing senior-mentor seat supervision from day 12 forward
notes: The kingdom's first catalyst-villain to be defeated by a procedural-handbook's own time-threshold rule (her primary procedural-response crossing the session-start threshold by 1 minute 43 seconds rendering the response procedurally invalid). The first catalyst-villain in the saga's registry to have a non-violent administrative-procedural-control as the chapter's primary mechanism of harm (the 147 silenced-poet rota-removals across 18 months; the Acharya Bharati's removal-and-natural-causes-death sequence; the Sangam Hall's standing-debate's 18-month pause). The kingdom-council's amended Sangam-charter's Seventh Clause's reassignment-to-archive provision is the kingdom's standing precedent for handling administrative-procedural-control catalyst-villains in subsequent kingdoms; the precedent applies to all kingdoms with authorisation-protocol weaponisation. Survives Ch 2.
